# Quick start

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://efference.net/install.sh | sh
```
<!-- TODO: the installer URL is generated by dist and does not exist yet. Confirm the exact command dist emits, what the installer writes besides the binary, and the release targets (macOS and Linux; no Windows). -->

efference runs on macOS and Linux. It needs `bash`, which runs the agent's commands. Git
is needed only for sessions that work in their own git worktree, a separate checkout of
the project.
<!-- src: src/bash.rs; src/worktree.rs; src/bin/efference/island.rs (std::os::unix); src/secrets.rs (macOS and Linux stores only) -->

## Run it in a project

```sh
cd ~/code/your-project
efference
```

The first time, efference asks how to reach a model. Each answer is a **connection**: a
provider — Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI, a ChatGPT subscription, or another endpoint that
speaks one of the same APIs — a name for it, and where its key comes from: an environment
variable, or pasted now and kept in your OS keychain. (A ChatGPT subscription signs in
through the browser instead.) The answers go to `~/.efference/config.toml`, which records
*where* each key is, not the key. [Credentials](credentials.md) explains the choices.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::default_verb, run; src/setup.rs::PROVIDERS; src/setup/flow.rs::one_connection, api_key_source, describe_endpoint; src/setup/flow/chatgpt.rs::chatgpt_source; src/setup/render.rs::HEADER -->

If the key is in an environment variable that isn't set in this shell, setup stops there
and says so. Set it and run `efference` again; [Credentials](credentials.md) shows how to
start efference under 1Password's `op run`.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::run -->

Next, if the project has no `efference.toml` — the file that holds a project's settings
for efference — it offers to set the project up: in this terminal, in your browser, or not
now. Setting up starts an agent **session**, an ordinary conversation with the model,
billed as normal use. You pick the model on a form first. The agent asks before reading
your files, asks what sessions here may do without asking you and what they should know,
and writes `efference.toml` (and an `AGENTS.md`, if the project has no agent guide). It
asks whose project this is, and keeps efference's own files out of version control to
match.
<!-- src: src/setup/handoff.rs::offer_project_setup; src/bin/efference/picker.rs::create_through_form; src/boot/scaffold.rs::CONFIG_SCAFFOLD; assets/guide/new-project.md -->

From then on, `efference` in that directory opens the new-session form, or a short menu
when there are sessions here already: attach to one that is running, or resume an earlier
one.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/setup.rs::default_verb; src/bin/efference/picker.rs::run, menu; src/bin/efference/picker/app.rs::ask -->

To add or change a connection later, run `efference setup`.
<!-- src: src/setup/flow.rs::run (existing connections -> manage::run) -->

## Keeping sessions running

Started this way, efference runs **standalone**: the session runs inside this terminal's
efference process, and quitting stops it. Its record is kept, and `efference` in the
project offers to resume it.
<!-- src: src/daemon/island.rs::OwnerWatch; src/bin/efference/picker.rs::resume_on -->

For sessions that keep working when you close the terminal interface, run a **host**, a
long-lived efference process that holds sessions, in a terminal you leave open:

```sh
efference --host
```

While it runs, `efference` in any project uses it, and quitting the terminal interface
detaches from the session instead of stopping it. [How efference runs](how-it-runs.md)
covers both modes and running a host as a service; [Remote access](remote-access.md)
covers turning on the web client for browsers, phones, and Tailscale.
<!-- src: src/bin/efference/cli.rs::host_candidates; src/tui/control_strip.rs::strip_live_items -->
